/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages):
    text=page.extract_text()
    (p/f'page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
    print(f'PAGE {i+1}: {len(text)} characters')
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'PAGE {i+1}\\n'+page.extract_text() for i,page in enumerate(r.pages)))
PY"

strengths: The mean-point correspondence is a simple, original, and useful approach to the difficult four-point, three-view pose problem. Reusing established five-point and P3P solvers makes the contribution accessible and practically relevant without requiring an exact algebraic solution.

The empirical support is substantial: 90,000 camera triplets across 18 scenes and three datasets, evaluated with both PoseLib and GC-RANSAC. Supplementary experiments investigate noise, viewing geometry, outliers, thresholds, and individual scenes. Evaluation using the maximum error across all three camera pairs also supports the main accuracy trend.

Table 2 demonstrates useful improvements against a strengthened baseline. On PhotoTourism, 4p3v(M)+R+F+ENM essentially matches 5pt+P3P+R+F+ENM accuracy (AUC@10 of 76.16 versus 76.20) while reducing runtime from 56.52 to 44.51 ms. The shifted variant raises AUC@10 to 77.14, demonstrating an additional accuracy option.

Ablations explain the importance of early refitting and fourth-point refinement rather than attributing all gains to the approximate correspondence. Parameters are validated on a separate scene, and a source-code link is provided. The clear core construction and extensive practical validation support weak acceptance despite the comparison limitations below.
weaknesses: The runtime comparison against the HC solver is confounded by initialization overhead. Section 8.3, footnote 8 reports loading weights/data once per RANSAC run, taking approximately 45 ms; Table 2 reports total HC runtimes of approximately 60–67 ms. Such loading can be amortized across triplets, so these measurements do not establish the claimed speed advantage for repeated estimation. Initialization and steady-state costs should be separated.

The strongest refined five-point baselines from Table 2 are absent from the speed–accuracy curves in Figure 4 and the alternative-metric comparison in Table 5. This limits the evidence for the claimed best trade-off. For example, the fully enhanced shifted solver achieves 77.14 versus 76.20 AUC@10 on PhotoTourism but takes 112.60 versus 56.52 ms. Matched-time comparisons against the enhanced baseline are needed to establish the extent of its advantage.

The theoretical support is limited to an image-space approximation bound. Lemma 1 bounds the mean-point epipolar error by the triangle extent, which can be large and does not control pose error or convergence of refinement. Figure 9 confirms residual bias even with noiseless correspondences. The method's reliability is therefore established primarily for the tested RANSAC pipelines, with weaker support for broader claims of negligible scene dependence.

Some reporting details need clarification: the precise refinement residual and pose parameterization, and the conversion from the affine fundamental matrix to a calibrated pose, are insufficiently specified for a self-contained implementation. Table 6 also repeats all Cambridge statistics between corresponding affine and mean-based +R+F variants, including their ENM versions. These are localized reproducibility and reporting concerns.
